articleHeadline: Molecular Survey Detects Widespread Zoonotic Parasites in Hubei Goat Herds
articleSummary: As of 2026-11-12, across five goat-farming regions in Hubei Province, China, a cross-sectional molecular survey of 500 fecal samples (April 2024–April 2025) found widespread circulation of Giardia duodenalis (29.4%), Enterocytozoon bieneusi (16.2%), and Cryptosporidium spp. (3.2%). Cryptosporidium positives (n=16) were mainly C. bovis (8) and C. xiaoi (6); zoonotic lineages included C. parvum IIdA19G1 and C. ubiquitum XIIa (one each, 6.3% of positives). Giardia and E. bieneusi harbored human-infective lineages as well, indicating cross-species transmission potential. Regionally, prevalence varied (e.g., Xiangyang 6.9%). Molecular work used nested PCR targeting multi-locus loci for Giardia, ITS for E. bieneusi, SSU rRNA and gp60 for Cryptosporidium, with BLAST and phylogenetic validation. Goats thus represent reservoirs with public-health implications.

articleSummary: Delhi, India-based prospective cohort study of 134 culture-confirmed rifampicin-resistant or multidrug-resistant TB index cases and 305 household contacts (July 2016–February 2018) found high concordance of drug resistance profiles and genetic strain patterns between index patients and infected household members. Among 19 culture-positive contacts, phenotypic drug susceptibility matched the corresponding index case in 18 pairs (94.7%; 95% CI 74.0–99.9). Spoligotype patterns matched in 18 of 19 pairs (94.7%; 95% CI 74.0–99.9%), with a Cohen’s kappa of 0.89. Genotyping revealed 14 spoligotype patterns across six major lineages; CAS1_DELHI and Beijing were predominant. Polyclonal infection occurred in 39 of 134 index cases (29.1%). Authors caution spoligotyping’s limited discriminatory power and cannot prove transmission, but findings support systematic household contact investigations for drug-resistant TB.

articleSummary: Thai Medical Council on Nov 12 cited 83% infection-free in a small randomized trial of mosnodenvir, an experimental dengue antiviral, as weekly pre-exposure prophylaxis, citing NEJM research. articleSummary: As of 12 November 2026, Brazil’s Anvisa suspended batch 180926 of Italy-branded sliced mozzarella from Agroindústria Santo Anjo Ltda after Listeria monocytogenes was found in 25 g of the sample (lab report 56058/2026). The sanitary measure blocks sale, distribution, advertising and use of the batch and includes a voluntary recall announced by the company; only this batch is implicated, not the entire product line. Consumers who bought the mozzarella should check the batch number 180926 and not consume the product if present, contacting the retailer or manufacturer for recall procedures. Listeria monocytogenes can survive refrigeration, underlining the need for strict hygiene, processing controls, and microbiological monitoring in ready-to-eat cheeses. Symptoms of listeriosis range from fever, muscle aches, nausea and diarrhea to meningitis or septicemia, with pregnant individuals, newborns, the elderly, and immunocompromised being most at risk. Regulatory context in Brazil includes RDC 724/2022 and IN 161/2022 for food microbiological standards.

articleSummary: Dengue, chikungunya, scrub typhus, and leptospirosis are dangerous fever-causing infections in children during the rainy and post-monsoon seasons. Dengue brings sudden high fever, headache, body/eye pain, and vomiting; abdominal pain, bleeding, or fatigue may occur and require monitoring as fever declines. Influenza causes fever with cough, sore throat, headache, and muscle pains; spread via droplets and may lead to pneumonia in young kids. Scrub typhus from field mites causes prolonged fever with headache and body pains; an eschar at the bite site may appear or not, and untreated infection can affect lungs, liver, or kidneys. Leptospirosis from contaminated water causes fever, muscle pain, headache, red eyes, and sometimes jaundice or kidney/brain involvement; floodwater exposure increases risk. Urgent signs include breathing difficulty, fainting, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, bleeding, or reduced urination; avoid self-medication and seek care; discuss influenza vaccination with a pediatrician.

articleHeadline: Fecal Bacteria Fail to Predict Persistent Protozoan Parasites in Brazilian
articleSummary: Giardia species and Cystoisospora species DNA persisted in southern Brazil’s Pelotas microregion (Rio Grande do Sul) across eight sites and four campaigns (Mar–Aug 2025) along urban drainage canals, receiving waters, a drinking-water reservoir, and a Patos Lagoon beach (Praia do Laranjal). Conventional fecal indicator E. coli showed strong temporal dynamics: high in dry periods (>300 CFU/100 mL) and near-zero by August (<1–4 CFU/100 mL), with E. coli negatively correlated with rainfall (rho −0.47) and positively with temperature (rho 0.73). In contrast, protozoan genetic markers did not mirror bacterial declines, remaining detectable despite rising turbidity (0.46–0.63 NTU) and cooler temperatures (13.5–21.1°C). Two-liter sample concentration and molecular screening revealed persistent parasite DNA across urban drainage networks and receiving waters, indicating substantial blind spots in monitoring approaches that rely on culturable E. coli and underscoring ongoing exposure risks in drinking-water, irrigation, and recreational contexts in southern Brazil.
